summary: Feed s176_triple is degraded with 3 faults: VLAN 20 completely missing (49% untagged), 5.1% TCP packet drops, and microbursts to 3.71 Gbps overloading the 1 Gbps SIEM port. Immediate broker fixes needed to restore complete visibility.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or upstream switch is stripping 802.1Q tags or trunk is misconfigured: required VLAN 20 is 0% present and 49% of packets arrive untagged. Likely broker ingress/egress set to access mode or 'strip VLAN' enabled instead of trunk retain-tag.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM has zero visibility into VLAN 20 segment and cannot filter/correlate by VLAN 10/20 as required. 49% untagged traffic breaks VLAN-based detection rules and tenant separation, creating blind spot for lateral movement in VLAN 20.

recommended_fix.why: Configure broker and source trunk to retain 802.1Q tags and forward VLANs 10 and 20 to SIEM so required segmentation is preserved for detection.

findings.root_cause: 5.1% of TCP packets (148/2896) show gaps/retransmissions indicating capture loss before the SIEM, consistent with SPAN/mirror buffer overflow during bursts rather than SIEM processing. Correlates with 3.71 Gbps bursts exceeding port capacity.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM receives incomplete TCP streams and flows; even though it doesn't need full payload, missing packets break stream reassembly and event correlation, causing missed alerts and incomplete forensic records.

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy without SPAN buffer drops, eliminating the 5% capture loss that SPAN incurs under burst load.

findings.root_cause: Aggregated feed bursts to 3.71 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 1 Gbps SIEM port (371% of capacity, 3 overloaded intervals). Single 1G tool port is undersized for the aggregated traffic volume.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM NIC buffers overrun and drops traffic indiscriminately during bursts, directly causing the observed packet drops and creating periodic complete blindness to attacks during peak bursts.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute 3.7 Gbps bursts across 4x1G or upgrade to 10G tool ports via broker load-balancing so SIEM can ingest peak rate without drops; SIEM tolerates sampling/filtering but currently needs capacity.
